_portComment: the reference is now the PUBLIC repository toppers/fmp3_esp_idf at its 2026-08-18 snapshot. That repository is a series of squashed snapshots, so its commit list cannot be compared with the private fmp3_esp_idf_dev history; compare trees instead. The previous baseline, 1683046b from the dev repository, is not reachable from the public one and has to be fetched by SHA.
_portPatchesComment: Empty on purpose. This port is not expressed as a patch series against the baseline: upstream has moved too far for the hunks to carry context, and the port itself was restructured. Treat the baseline commit above as provenance, not as something these sources can be regenerated from.

entries._comment: the dual-core profile is gone (m5-unified now builds the SMP kernel), and a shipped stage has no PRC2 task, so this example cannot demonstrate anything a user could reproduce. It stays in the repository as the input to Test-Smp.ps1, which builds it against phase6_smp_selftest. Ship it again once sketches can place their own task on PRC2.

M5Core only: the ESP32-S3 has no BR/EDR radio, so the CoreS3 and StickS3 boards have no Bluetooth Classic (SPP) runtime option. It ships anyway, because packaging/README.release.md points users at this example by name and the three boards share one architecture - Arduino cannot offer a library example for one board out of three. The example itself refuses to compile on the other two with a sentence saying which board to pick, rather than failing at the link.

a test fixture, not something to hand a user: it deliberately never calls M5.begin(), because it exists to prove that an Arduino-compiled object can take the address of the FMP3-linked M5 and be linked into the image. Test-M5UnifiedLink.ps1 builds it and Test-Hardware.ps1 flashes what that produces. Listed here with boardsManager false, the same way DualCore is, so that its absence is a statement rather than an omission - make_package_index.py now rejects an example that appears in neither.

_releaseArtifactsComment: a release is three kinds of artifact, not one. The platform archive carries the board definition, the prebuilt stages and the bundled library; the link driver is a separate Arduino tool frozen once per host, because a sketch build needs it and no package index ships a Python interpreter. scripts/check_release_artifacts.py verifies an assembled release against this section before it is published.

linkDriver._hostsComment: Arduino host triplets a release must carry a frozen driver for. x86_64-apple-darwin is absent on purpose: the macos-13 runner stopped being allocated, and a queued job hangs rather than fails, so it would stall the release. Intel Macs cannot build with 0.3.0. Add the host back here and in both workflows once a working Intel label exists.
